reasons.plausibility: The hypothesis is physically sound, linking controlled diffusion-driven precipitation to a protective passive layer, but it assumes Mg–Zn or Mg–Ti precipitates will form and be protective without addressing the well-known high reactivity and non-protective nature of Mg-rich oxides in many alloy systems.
reasons.testability: The proposed test is clear and decisive, with a well-defined falsification criterion based on comparing precipitate distribution and passive film quality between slow-annealed and quenched samples using appropriate characterization techniques.
reasons.usefulness: The hypothesis is highly useful as it proposes a direct, testable pathway to control corrosion/oxidation resistance in a challenging alloy class, though the specific precipitate chemistry is speculative and would need refinement.
